title: Scrapbook: school band and the Optimist Jazzers lineup
summary: A school band photo, a Mardi Gras picnic, and his best men Earl Christian and Bill Voorhees.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: And I see a picture of you with a big band.

That was a school band and we had to use everybody in the school. We couldn't get any ringers. But you had a few good musicians there. This King guy used to arrange for a blue opera, one of them. Dr. Fatter on the tuba. You know Dr. Fatter was in the Clay Shaw case? No, I heard about him.

Yeah, and the drum player couldn't play at all. The piano player was pretty good. The trombone players with Schroeder, George, they read good in the Singleton. They couldn't read anything but they couldn't play all the music. I got a tape on it and I sound pretty good in that band.
This is the band all went to that elementary school? All of the children did, yeah. Oh, all of the children.

Cheerleaders picnic in 1950 at Audubon Park. For the handicapped. They could charge you in those days every once in a while. Goodwill had a party at Lyons Center. You know our time is running out. I've got a... That girl's name is Joyce Mayo there. The one that sang with you? Yeah, I don't know her name. Yeah, well you wouldn't remember her but I know her ex-husband.
That was a good band. Monk Hayes and Lou Cheek Morton two of my best men. I wish he could see them. I'd love to have that picture if it was complete.
Yeah, I could see Charlie Hartman and Chris on the tune. That's right. Christian, Earl Christian. And then your piano player.
Bill Voorhees, the old Maple Leaf Ragman. That's what we call him, the Maple Leaf Ragman. And we have a tape with this band here on the other side.
